reason: Materialize the already-implemented V21 Personal Access authority for real release use without redesigning licensing or Matrix identity. Existing source already proves OWNER permanent use, TESTER request/grant lifecycle, installation binding, fail-closed Product API enforcement, Cloudflare Worker + D1 request/grant authority, and secure owner-secret custody. The remaining causal gap is production materialization: the Worker/D1 deployment is still placeholder-only, the sealed release platform-auth authority has no Personal Access URL, Electron does not project a sealed Personal Access authority URL into the backend child, and the OWNER machine has not yet been provisioned with the matching owner-admin secret. This batch reuses the existing Worker/D1 implementation, existing Wrangler CLI, existing sealed platform-auth release resource and existing Desktop CredentialVault application coordinator; it adds no second identity, entitlement, configuration, secret-storage, deployment-state, or cryptographic mechanism.

localRemoteMaterialization: Apply the existing D1 migration to one real yance-personal-access database.
Set one cryptographically random OWNER_ADMIN_SECRET as a Cloudflare Worker secret; never print or commit it.
Deploy the existing Worker through Wrangler and obtain one real HTTPS authority URL.
Seal that exact HTTPS URL into platform-auth.json and detached SHA-256 release resources.
Provision the same OWNER secret into the OWNER Windows CredentialVault under personal-access.owner-admin through the existing desktop credential application authority.
Prove OWNER usable, fresh TESTER request pending, owner approve -> ACTIVE, different installation denied, suspend/revoke denied, and remote failure never promotes TESTER.

retireOrAvoid: Do not create another licensing/entitlement backend.
Do not reopen Matrix public registration or use Matrix accounts as Personal Access truth.
Do not introduce a second release configuration file for Personal Access.
Do not pass OWNER_ADMIN_SECRET through platform-auth.json, URLs, logs, GitHub files or plaintext SQLite.
Do not add custom D1 migration, retry, secret-storage or deployment-state mechanisms where Wrangler and existing repository authorities already exist.
Do not implement hardware fingerprinting or strong DRM in this batch.
